paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The changes in Efficacytop (the rate of successfully maximizing the object's probability) and noise_E with the number of edits. The top figure displays results for GPT2-XL using AlphaEdit and MEMIT, while the bottom figure shows results for LLaMA3-8B using only AlphaEdit. MEMIT is excluded for LLaMA3-8B due to its excessively high noise_E, making visualization difficult.
model_annotation: The line chart illustrates the variation of Efficacy_top (left y-axis) and noise_E (right y-axis) as functions of the number of edits (x-axis) for the GPT2-XL model, comparing two methods: AlphaEdit and MEMIT. The x-axis is linear, ranging from 0 to 3000 edits with tick marks at 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, and 3000. The left y-axis, labeled “Efficacy_top,” is linear, spanning from 0 to 100 with major ticks at intervals of 10. The right y-axis, labeled “noise_E,” is linear, ranging from 0 to 140 with major ticks at intervals of 20. Four lines are plotted: AlphaEdit Efficacy_top (red dashed line with square markers) starts at approximately 100 at 500 edits and declines gradually to about 86 at 3000 edits; AlphaEdit noise_E (red solid line with circle markers) begins near 0 at 500 edits and rises slightly to about 18 at 3000 edits; MEMIT Efficacy_top (light blue dashed line with square markers) begins at 88 at 500 edits, peaks at 100 near 1000 edits, then declines sharply to 25 at 3000 edits; MEMIT noise_E (light blue solid line with circle markers) starts near 0 at 500 edits, increases steadily to 140 at 3000 edits, with a notable inflection point around 2000 edits where it accelerates upward.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of edits (x-axis, ranging from 0 to 3000 with tick marks at 500-unit intervals) and two performance metrics — Efficacy_top (left y-axis, linear scale from 0 to 100) and noise_E (right y-axis, linear scale from 0 to 140) — for the GPT2-XL model under two editing methods: AlphaEdit and MEMIT. For AlphaEdit, Efficacy_top (red dashed line with square markers) starts near 100 and gradually declines to approximately 86 by 3000 edits, while its noise_E (solid red line with circular markers) remains consistently low, hovering around 20–30 across all edit counts. In contrast, MEMIT’s Efficacy_top (light blue dashed line with square markers) begins at ~88, drops steadily to ~25 by 3000 edits, while its noise_E (solid light blue line with circular markers) starts near 0, rises sharply after 1500 edits, and peaks at ~140 by 3000 edits. The dual y-axis design allows simultaneous visualization of efficacy decay and noise accumulation, revealing that MEMIT incurs significantly higher noise over time compared to AlphaEdit, despite similar initial efficacy.
